Cookie Policy

v2.0 · updated on May 8, 2026

This page details, technically and nominally, all cookies and similar technologies used in our fields, in accordance with the ANPD Cookie Guide (out/2023, revision 2024), GDPR and ePrivacy Directive. For the overview, see Privacy Policy.

What are cookies?

Cookies are small text files that websites store in your browser to remember information between visits — preferences, sessions, metrics. Similar technologies include local storage, session storage, web beacons and fingerprinting. For the purposes of this policy, all are treated equally.

Categories we use

  • Required   Essential to navigation, authentication and Security. Always active.
  • Analysis   Aggregated metrics (traffic, pages plus visited, time). Opt-in.
  • Marketing   Campaign measurement and remarketing. Opt-in.
  • Customization   Memories of preferences interface. Opt-in.

How to manage your preferences

  • Use consent banner who appears on the first visit.
  • Anytime, click on icon in the lower left corner to reopen the preferences.
  • Configure in your browser total blocking of third party cookies — information on About cookies. org.
  • If your browser sends the signal Global Privacy Control (GPC), we respect automatically as marketing opt-out/analysis.

Lock at source (Consent Mode v2)

We implemented the Google Consent Mode v2 as required by March/2024. Before any Your decision, all non-essential categories remain in denied. Analysis and marketing tags only fire after explicit consent or only send pings no cookies (model mode).

Third party cookies and jurisdictions

Operators like Google and Meta can set additional cookies by accessing integrated content (videos from YouTube, maps, embeds). These providers are responsible for their own cookies — see:

  • Google: Police. google.com/technologies/cookies
  • Target: facebook. with/policies/cookies
  • YouTube: Police. google.com/privacy

Changes in this policy

We review the listing every six months or whenever there is change in third parties. Material changes reopen the consent banner.
